Summarize a topic-count comparison

Source: R/accessors.R
summary.sbert_topic_sweep.Rd

summary() reduces a comparison of candidate numbers of topics to one row per segment level: the range of numbers compared, the number with the highest mean coherence, that candidate's diversity and between-topic variance, and whether every candidate converged. The full table of candidates is given by as.data.frame().

Coherence is one guide among several; the choice of a number of topics should also rest on reading the representative texts of the candidates.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sbert_topic_sweep'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A comparison returned by compare_topics().

...

Ignored.

Value

A data frame of class summary.sbert_topic_sweep with one row per segment level and columns segment, n_candidates, min_topics, max_topics, best_n_topics (highest coherence; NA when no candidate can be scored), coherence, topic_diversity, explained, and all_converged. It prints as a table.

See also

compare_topics(), plot(), fitted().

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
comparison <- compare_topics(corpus, n_topics = c(4, 6, 8),
                             column = "translation",
                             embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
summary(comparison)
#> Topic-count comparison: highest mean npmi coherence per level
#> 
#>   segment n_candidates min_topics max_topics best_n_topics coherence
#>  document            3          4          8             6    -0.104
#>  topic_diversity explained all_converged
#>            0.917     0.226          TRUE
